sections.markdown:
## C — Knowledge dossier: Night, work zones, winter and rural driving

FACT_ID: sec18-F01 | anchor: A66
Night driving is more hazardous because the headlights limit how far ahead the driver can see. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F02 | anchor: A66
The handbook recommends high beams without oncoming traffic but low beams when following another vehicle. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F03 | anchor: A66
Dim for oncoming traffic and look toward the right edge if another vehicle’s high beams create glare. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F04 | anchor: A66
Use low beams in fog, rain or snow, with fitted fog lights as available, because high-beam reflection can reduce visibility. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F05 | anchor: A66
Avoid staring into approaching headlights and keep scanning the road ahead. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F06 | anchor: A66
Look ahead for dark road shapes and occasionally check both edges for hazards from the sides. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F07 | anchor: A66
Avoid tinted eyewear, including sunglasses and colored lenses, during nighttime or overcast-day driving because the tint reduces vision. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F08 | anchor: A66
For night driving, add at least 1 second to the following interval. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F09 | anchor: A66
On an unfamiliar road at night, the handbook calls for at least 2 additional following seconds. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F10 | anchor: A66
A work zone is a roadwork area that may include closed lanes, detours or moving equipment. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F11 | anchor: A66
The handbook reports about 40,000 yearly injuries from work-zone vehicle crashes. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F12 | anchor: A66
Before entering a work zone, look for workers and large vehicles along with barrels, cones and signs; its warning signs have orange backgrounds with black words or symbols. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F13 | anchor: A66
Reduce speed in a work zone even without workers because narrow lanes and rough pavement remain hazards. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F14 | anchor: A66
Obey work-zone speed signs, noting that speeding fines may be doubled. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F15 | anchor: A66
Watch digital work-zone messages as well as ordinary signs because they can warn of changing conditions or slow and stopped traffic. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F16 | anchor: A66
In a work zone, increase following room, monitor nearby traffic and prepare to stop. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F17 | anchor: A66
At night in a work zone, use extra caution whether or not workers are visible. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F18 | anchor: A66
Adjust lane position to leave room for road workers and construction vehicles. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F19 | anchor: A66
Continue following work-zone signs until reaching End Road Work. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec18-F20 | anchor: A66
Plan for work-zone delays by leaving early and choosing an alternative route when possible. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0066]

Misconceptions: No workers present does not make a work zone hazard-free; the snowplow distance applies at its stated posted-limit and flashing-light conditions; generic winter brake wording must not replace vehicle-specific ABS instructions.
Mnemonics: Use light, surface, space and sight as an authored special-condition cue.
Glossary: A work zone may change lanes or routes; gravel and bridge gratings reduce grip; an uncontrolled intersection lacks stop or yield signs.
Dynamic facts: Weather, road closures, work zones and equipment change continuously. No current closure or personal vehicle configuration is inferred from the handbook.
